## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dīpijātaka* (Ja 426) is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection, positioned within the *Kaccānivagga* of the *Aṭṭhanipāta* [Fausböll 1883]. According to the traditional framework, the Buddha related this story while residing at Jetavana with reference to a certain she-goat. The narrative features an interaction between a she-goat (*eḷikā*) and a panther (*dīpi* / *dīpika*), observed by an ascetic (*tāpaso*); in the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies himself as having been that ascetic [Fausböll 1883]. The text is cataloged with verse selections in modern collections such as that of Ānandajoti [Ānandajoti 2010].
